There was a time, a couple of years ago, when it was rumoured a double Champions League winner was Eddie Howe’s probable replacement at Newcastle. Rubbish, according to some close to the club: they were not going for Jose Mourinho. Instead, after Howe has gone now, a double Asian Champions League winner is taking over, in Matthias Jaissle.

Young, German, relatively unknown and an advocate of pressing, Jaissle represents a very different kind of appointment. The second manager brought in since Newcastle’s Saudi takeover, the 38-year-old joins a club at a crossroads; one interpretation is that they are changing direction, another that they are going backwards.

open image in gallery Matthias Jaissle looks set to be the next Newcastle manager ( Getty )

Brilliant a job as Howe did, the scale of the task Jaissle inherits does not merely reflect the difficulty of following the first manager to take a domestic trophy to Tyneside since the 1950s or of managing expectations.

When Newcastle start their season against Liverpool, they will almost certainly be without the four players of most pedigree who started the equivalent fixture last August: Kieran Trippier and Anthony Gordon, the only Englishmen to score in World Cup semi-finals since 1990, and Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, Newcastle’s two classiest midfielders in decades.

open image in gallery Bruno Guimaraes (left) looks set to follow Anthony Gordon out of Newcastle ( Getty )

Guimaraes’ probable move to Arsenal, following Tonali’s £100m transfer to Tottenham and Gordon’s £69m switch to Barcelona, will create multiple holes. Part of Jaissle’s job will be one of persuasion: ensuring that three big sales this summer, after the veteran Trippier left when his contract expired, do not become a rush to the exits, with players such as Lewis Hall and Tino Livramento following.

A side that had a surfeit of leaders could soon look short of them. Dan Burn is the logical successor to Guimaraes as captain, even if the long-term ideal may be to pair Sven Botman with Malick Thiaw in the heart of the defence. But as Newcastle overdoes it on youth, there are few other alternatives as skipper.

open image in gallery Dan Burn could be Newcastle’s next captain ( PA Wire )

A midfield that ranked among the best is no more, with the departure of the two most stylish components, only Joelinton remaining and questions if he may be in decline. The arrivals of 20-year-old Aladji Bamba and 18-year-old Sean Steur show Newcastle have started to build their next-gen midfield; but each has only had a season of regular first-team football. They are long-term acquisitions, but Newcastle will have short-term imperatives. Some sort of unit is required: the precocious Lewis Miley should be in it, but there are doubts about Joe Willock’s future and Jacob Ramsey had an underwhelming first year in the north-east.

And even with high-calibre players, Newcastle were reliant on Guimaraes. Since he broke into the team in 2022, they only won two league games without the Brazilian. He was their top scorer in the top flight last season and their talisman.

open image in gallery Newcastle have been reliant upon Bruno Guimaraes ( PA Wire )

In attack, Jaissle is confronted with the problem that seemed to confound Howe: what to do with the £125m duo who were bought with the proceeds of Alexander Isak’s sale. Had Howe stayed, the probability was that Will Osula would have started the season as the first-choice striker, not the £55m Yoane Wissa or the £69m Nick Woltemade. The Congolese had a good World Cup but scored one goal in 19 league games for Newcastle; the German sometimes ended up as a No 10 or a No 8 under Howe during a spell of one in 26 in all competitions.

Anthony Elanga was a third unsuccessful attacking addition last summer, though, like Wissa, he showed some of his ability at the World Cup. Gordon’s sale should at least resolve a problem Newcastle created for themselves: he and Harvey Barnes were both best suited to the left flank and now the latter, perhaps the best finisher at the club, should be starting, though the £42m Bazoumana Toure has also arrived.

open image in gallery Harvey Barnes could be given a bigger role after the departure of Anthony Gordon ( PA )

But he is one of four newcomers who cost more than £100m between them but are aged 18 or 20; Newcastle’s change in recruitment policy may have been enforced by financial regulations, and a Uefa fine for breaching spending caps, but it means that both they need to improve the emerging talents they have bought and get results in the meantime.

In goal, it is notable that Howe’s perennial target James Trafford has eluded them; enter Ewen Jaouen and, probably, Lukas Hornicek, the latter seemingly to start and presumably to prompt Nick Pope’s exit.

But the rebuilding feels unfinished: with Trippier going, they lack alternatives to Hall and Livramento in the full-back roles. With Guimaraes going, they may need another midfielder. For now, centre-back may be the only position where Newcastle have both proven quality and quantity.

Elsewhere, they have imported potential but have ended up selling successful signings and keeping some so far unsuccessful ones. Howe ultimately joined the ranks of managers who constructed one terrific team but not a second at the same club. Whatever the current squad becomes, for now the starting 11 could look Newcastle’s weakest since Howe kept them up in 2022.

open image in gallery Howe leaves a weakening Newcastle squad behind ( PA Wire )

They come off a demoralising second half of last season, are further jolted by Howe’s decision to step away and begin the campaign with potentially chastening reunions with Isak and Tonali. There is a lot that could go wrong.

The counter-argument is that much has gone right in Jaissle’s coaching career. Newcastle can look at his win percentages with Liefering, RB Salzburg and Al-Ahli – 64, 68 and 65 respectively – and hope for something similar.

open image in gallery Matthias Jaissle boasts a strong record but has taken a tough job ( PA Wire )

But the warnings come from their own history. Newcastle can seem dependent on the minority of managers who can galvanise a club and a region. After Kevin Keegan left (the first time), they finished in the bottom half in each of the next four full seasons. After Bobby Robson’s sacking, they did that year and in three of the next four. Howe’s reign ended in the anti-climax of 12th place, and Jaissle takes on a team that has then been stripped of its stars, deprived of its manager and plunged into transition.

More than one in 10 householders who are currently living with a hosepipe ban do not intend to abide by it, according to a survey.

Some 11% of households said they did not intend to fully abide by the ban – while 5% said they did not yet know, the YouGov poll of more than 4,200 adults commissioned by the Press Association found.

Some 10% of householders said they would report a neighbour using a hose in their garden while a ban was in place and 71% said they would not, with the remainder unsure.

Seven water companies – Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Southern Water, South East Water, Thames Water and South West Water – have introduced the restrictions – officially known as a “Temporary Use Ban” – affecting 23 million customers, or around 40% of England’s population.

open image in gallery (PA Graphics) ( PA Graphics )

Overall, just half of households (49%) said they supported a hosepipe ban in their local area, while 35% said they opposed the restrictions.

A significant number of responses from those polled involved the belief that those on a meter should be able to use as much water as they needed because they were paying for it.

Other reasons given for ignoring a ban were concerns about fruit and vegetables going to waste because they were too difficult to water with a watering can, and to support wildlife in the garden.

Households subject to a ban can use a watering can, and using a hosepipe is still allowed to water food crops at home or on an allotment when using a watering can is not practical.

A drip irrigation system for a garden is also allowed as long as it is fitted with a timer and pressure-reducing valve and delivers water directly to the soil rather than spraying it into the air.

The ban does extend to using a hosepipe to clean a car or fill a paddling pool or domestic swimming pool.

open image in gallery Cricketers play on small patches of green grass surrounded by scorched earth at Hackney Marshes, east London (Ben Whitley/PA) ( PA Wire )

Other householders raised concerns about their water supplier’s wider performance, with one saying: “I pay an extortionate amount for my water. It is not my problem that water companies would rather give their CEOs ridiculous amounts of money instead of building new reservoirs.”

Another said: “How does a first world nation not have the infrastructure to support no rain for a month?”

The bans come as almost a third of England – including parts of the South East, Midlands and North West – languish in “prolonged dry weather” status, with only the North East and Yorkshire still seeing “normal” conditions for the time of year.

Last week, the Environment Agency declared seven areas of central, eastern and southern England – around half of the country – as officially in drought as a result of very low rainfall and high temperatures.

Last year, Yorkshire Water reported savings of up to 10% in household consumption when their hosepipe ban was in place, while Anglian Water has reported a 9% reduction in demand since its ban was implemented last month.

A Water UK spokeswoman said: “We are incredibly grateful to customers for doing their bit to protect our environment and preserve our water supplies.

“Some parts of the country have seen demand for water rise by more than a third.

“Water companies are working round the clock fixing leaks, moving water across regions and running treatment works flat out to keep supplies flowing, and we urge all customers to use water wisely.”

An Environment Agency spokeswoman said: “A hosepipe can use 1,000 litres an hour – which is more than a family-of-four will use in a day.

“These short-term bans allow companies to conserve their supplies as we don’t know when this drought will end.

“We are grateful to people for following the restrictions, where in place. The less water we use, the more stays in the local environment, which is vital for the health of our rivers and wildlife.”

Consumer Council for Water chief executive Mike Keil said: “We know hosepipe restrictions are frustrating for some people, but water companies have a duty to act when sustained hot, dry weather and increased demand for water threaten both the environment and the security of water supplies needed for essential use.

“However, asking customers to play their part means water companies must be playing theirs too. Water saving is a shared responsibility and when customers see their water company failing to get a grip on leakage, it understandably drains their own motivation to save water.”

Jeremy Clarkson has claimed that he’ll work between 15 and 20 hours a day on Diddly Squat in the summer – and yet, he doesn’t “actually get paid” for what he harvests.

The Clarkson’s Farm star, who originally bought his Cotswolds farm in 2008, began running it himself in 2019 and has since been vocal about the difficulties of making a profit as a farmer. Last month, he revealed that it’s become “impossible” to make money from growing food on the farm.

In his latest newspaper column, Clarkson shed more light on farm life, revealing that he’ll “work non-stop” on Diddly Squat in the summer and yet it’s still “cheaper to go on an expensive holiday”.

Writing in The Sun, he said that farmers are not able to book a summer holiday as it’s “impossible” to know when the harvest will be. “This means the farmer is forced to stay at home for the summer, looking at Instagram pictures of all his non-farming friends as they frolic on boats and in bars in the sun-drenched Mediterranean.

open image in gallery Clarkson shared the ‘unpleasant’ reality of working on a farm ( Prime Video )

“Sounds terrible, yes? Well it isn’t. Some jobs on the farm are unpleasant. Sexing rabbits is annoyingly difficult, and disposing of dead piglets is heartbreaking. But I’ve been harvesting all week, and this job is an absolute joy.”

He added that he wakes up at 4am to “work non-stop for 15 to 20 hours at a stretch” and while it’s “hot and dirty out there”, he can’t get enough of it.

“Finally, you turn off the engines and in the golden-hour silence that results, you crack open an ice cold bottle of beer and gulp at it as the sun goes down. I’ve drunk beers in many exotic and beautiful locations over the years, but none of them match the beer you treat yourself to after a hard day’s harvesting,” he said.

“The only slight fly in the ointment is that thanks to the hot summer and this Government’s strange hatred of farmers, you don’t actually get paid for the wheat and the barley you’ve harvested. In fact, I worked out this morning that it’d be cheaper to go on an expensive holiday.”

The Independent has contacted the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs for comment.

open image in gallery Jeremy Clarkson with his partner Lisa Hogan, pictured in 2024 ( Getty )

Last month, Clarkson called for action from the government on farming matters, revealing that he’s left 200 acres of his farm bare as it would be “impossible” to make money from it. “We knew that if we planted it with wheat or barley, we would definitely make a loss,” he said.

Since taking up farming, Clarkson has become actively engaged with agricultural policy; in May 2024, he challenged government planning reforms, advocating for farmers to convert agricultural buildings into homes and shops.

Meanwhile, in the last series of Clarkson’s Farm, viewers watched as the presenter protested against the government’s proposals to increase inheritance tax by 20 per cent on agricultural assets worth more than £1m. After the protests, the government increased the threshold from £1m to £2.5m.

The recent series also saw Clarkson reveal that he had been diagnosed with cancer. He shared on the show that his cancer was aggressive but had been caught at a “really early” stage, and later said that a post-treatment test two months ago found no indication of cancer.

The race for the Ballon d’Or is entering its final stretch after the world’s best players made significant statements during the 2026 World Cup.

Eight-time winner Lionel Messi showed that, at 39, he could still force himself into the conversation, firing eight goals to propel Argentina to the final and briefly take the crown as the competition’s all-time top goalscorer - until he was eclipsed by Kylian Mbappe.

However, Spain’s triumph over Argentina in the finale will surely bode well for the likes of 2024 winner Rodri and Lamine Yamal in their pursuit of the individual accolade, who will look to start the new club season with some spellbinding performances to complement their part in winning football’s most coveted trophy.

Harry Kane was the favourite for the Ballon d’Or before this summer after his sublime goalscoring campaign with Bayern Munich - can he replicate that unparalleled form in the early months of 2026/27 to make team achievements irrelevant come October’s ceremony?

Here’s how the top 10 front-runners stack up in The Independent’s Ballon d’Or 2026 power rankings:

1. Rodri

open image in gallery Rodri won the Golden Ball at the World Cup to stamp his mark on the Ballon d’Or race ( AP )

You might not like it, but the weight of the World Cup in the eyes of the Ballon d’Or jury is undeniable. Just ask Luka Modric.

Rodri had a sensational World Cup at the heart of Spain’s midfield, shielding their rock-solid defence while acting as the metronome that took play forward. His influence took him to the Golden Ball ahead of top goalscorers Messi and Mbappe - and we feel like that could be the precursor to him bringing home a second Ballon d’Or in October.

That would feel like a bit of an injustice, considering he didn’t have the most spectacular domestic season. Returning from injury with Manchester City, it took him a while to properly find his feet in a campaign that saw Pep Guardiola’s side win the FA Cup and League Cup, but miss out on the Premier League title. But the World Cup is the World Cup - and whether you agree with the importance of team achievements in an individual award, the reality is that it does matter a hell of a lot.

His pursuit of a second crown in three years could hinge on his recovery from minor back surgery, and then a possible move to Real Madrid. If he carries his World Cup form and inspires a lightning start to the season at the Santiago Bernabeu, that spotlight could be what swings the jury in his favour.

2. Harry Kane

open image in gallery Harry Kane scored 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern last term ( Getty )

England captain Kane is still the odds-on favourite to win the Ballon d’Or despite failing to set the World Cup alight quite like he managed the Bundesliga in 2025/26. That’s a testament to just how prolific he was last term.

Kane was the top goalscorer in Europe, hitting 61 goals in 51 games across all competitions as he spearheaded Bayern towards the league and cup double; he’s added silverware to his ever-present individual numbers. He was then hardly irrelevant at the World Cup, scoring six goals - including a crucial late brace against DR Congo to spare his country serious embarrassment - as England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966.

If his club form continues into the new campaign, the jury may have to put their emphasis on the World Cup and wider team achievement to one side.

3. Lamine Yamal

open image in gallery Lamine Yamal has now won both a European Championship and World Cup before turning 20 ( PA )

And back to the World Cup superiority complex we go, sort of. Yamal will surely win his fair share of Ballon d’Ors across his career, but the 19-year-old could very well end up taking home his first this year, going one better than his runners-up finish in 2025.

Yamal became the first player under 20 to appear at both a European Championship final and a World Cup final - he won both. While his output was pretty modest for his standards, he was influential throughout the tournament for Spain - and that’s after coming into it carrying a hamstring injury.

He also bagged 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona in another LaLiga-winning season - hardly a mediocre year for the teenager. He’s more than in with a shout.

4. Kylian Mbappe

open image in gallery Kylian Mbappe became the World Cup’s all-time record goalscorer this summer ( Reuters )

It feels pretty crazy to think that, at 27, Mbappe still doesn’t have a Ballon d’Or to his name, given he’s been at the top of the game for what feels like forever now.

Once again, he’s very much in the mix this time around. His Golden Boot at the World Cup will do most of the heavy lifting, with his 10 goals in North America seeing him pass first Miroslav Klose and then Lionel Messi as the tournament’s all-time record goalscorer. Both he and Messi would have felt hard done by not to go home with the Golden Ball.

But lest we forget, despite the toxicity that surrounded his club season with Real Madrid, he didn’t exactly experience a drop-off in performance. He bagged 42 goals in 44 games, all while being hounded at the Bernabeu - and while it wasn’t enough to prevent another trophyless season for Los Blancos, you can’t knock his output.

If he can get along with Jose Mourinho and get 2026/27 off to a flyer, he could well shoot up to the pinnacle of these rankings.

5. Lionel Messi

open image in gallery Lionel Messi, 39, is still in the mix after a stunning World Cup ( PA Wire )

He couldn’t again, could he? Messi’s inclusion on this list encapsulates the significance of the World Cup in deciding the Ballon d’Or winner; he’s not going to take the accolade for his MLS exploits, is he. But fair play to the eight-time winner; at 39, he showed he very much still had it.

Messi’s eight goals propelled Argentina to the World Cup final, where they were rightly defeated by Spain - had he lifted back-to-back titles, he’d probably be towards the top two of this list. After all, he claimed the 2023 award after La Albiceleste’s triumph 10 months earlier, by which time he was on the books at Inter Miami.

Even with his runners-up medal, Indy Sport writers had him as the player of the tournament. That, combined with the jury’s historic love for the Argentinian, means you can’t exactly write him off.

6. Ousmane Dembele

open image in gallery Ousmane Dembele won back-to-back Champions Leagues with PSG ( PA )

Had France won the World Cup, as many expected them to do leading up to that drab semi-final exit, Dembele would have been heavily favoured to secure a second successive Ballon d’Or. The combination of World Cup and Champions League winners’ medals is a bit of a cheat code.

That would’ve been quite the gimme for a player who, let’s be honest, was France’s fourth best attacker at the World Cup. And while, like last year, he ended the season as Paris Saint-Germain’s top scorer with a Ligue 1 and Champions League to boot, he only managed about half of his goalscoring output.

His trophy haul still carries enough weight to be comfortably in the top 10 contenders, but the failure to lift that World Cup title gives him only an outside chance to go back-to-back - and we think that’s fair.

Sorry Ousmane, but this year shouldn’t be your year.

7. Erling Haaland

open image in gallery Erling Haaland ripped open defences on his World Cup debut ( Getty )

He had us all doing the row.

Their first World Cup since 1998, Haaland ensured Norway lived up to their dark-horse status by powering them to the last-eight. On the way, his unrelenting goalscoring exploits humbled Brazil, sending the five-time winners packing. Away from the big-hitting nations, Haaland was far and away the tournament’s standout player, to little surprise.

Add that to a pretty bog-standard Haaland season for City - just the 38 goals last year, the fourth season he’s hit 30+ at the Etihad - which saw him lift a domestic double. Legacy-defining stats for nearly anyone else, but normal service for the big Norwegian.

As prolific as he may be, he’s currently a definite outsider in the Ballon d’Or race. That may change if he emulates the start to the season he had last year, which saw him smack home 13 in his first 10 league outings. Recency bias can be a powerful thing...

8. Jude Bellingham

open image in gallery Jude Bellingham silenced his critics at the World Cup ( Reuters )

How was this man’s place on the England plane ever in question?! Thomas Tuchel’s player of the tournament, Bellingham served his critics a serious helping of humble pie by guiding the Three Lions to the elusive World Cup bronze.

That beautiful redemption arc, on its own, has Bellingham on this list. That’s because the season that preceded the World Cup wasn’t spectacular. Injuries limited him to just 13 goal contributions for Real Madrid in another trophyless campaign.

It’s why his chances of winning the Ballon d’Or are still low compared to the competition. But as was proved in North America - don’t count him out.

9. Michael Olise

open image in gallery Michael Olise has proved himself as one of the world’s best attackers ( Getty )

Crystal Palace could only keep him in Croydon for so long.

With Bayern Munich and France, Olise has established himself as one of the world’s best attackers, a talent so bright that the German giants are doing all they can to ward off interest from the likes of Real Madrid - who no doubt saw the World Cup partnership he formed with Mbappe and want to reunite the pair in the Spanish capital.

Will his electrifying performances be enough to win the Ballon d’Or? Probably not, this year. But he’s in the conversation, which is a statement in itself.

10. Vinicius Jr

open image in gallery Vinicius Jr could be on the move to Arsenal this summer ( PA Wire )

Vinicius squeezes into our Ballon d’Or power rankings, mainly to spare myself some angry emails from those affiliated to Real Madrid, Brazil, and now maybe Arsenal. I joke, kind of.

The 2024 runner-up had another strong season at the Bernabeu, netting 22 goals in 36 appearances, though like Mbappe was unable to inspire the club to a trophy.

Similar could be said about his World Cup; he was one of the few bright lights in a wooden Brazil side under Carlo Ancelotti, which eventually succumbed to Haaland and co.

Could a move to the Emirates spark life into his Ballon d’Or bid?

News.content:

When Julia Rockwell and her husband, Steve, retired and downsized to a bungalow in Little Clapton, Essex, a little over a year ago, they weren't planning on joining the green energy revolution. But moving to a new neighbourhood changed everything. One of their new neighbours had already embraced solar power, and his enthusiasm proved infectious.

“Initially we were quite sceptical about solar panels,” Julia admits. “We had this idea that they were expensive, high-maintenance, and probably wouldn't deliver on their promises.”

Intrigued by their neighbour's first-hand success, the couple decided to get a quote from Octopus Energy. Even as they weighed up the decision, they harboured lingering doubts – particularly regarding the upfront cost – while some of their friends remained firmly unconvinced. Ultimately, they decided to take the plunge, installing 17 panels on their roof.

Harnessing the Essex sunshine

Installed on their south-facing roof in just a few days, the couple’s 17 solar panels have turned their energy bills into credit ( Octopus Energy )

“When we bought the bungalow, we were specifically looking for a south-facing garden,” Julia says. “As it turned out, that made the house absolutely ideal for solar. We have a large, uninterrupted south-facing roof, which allows us to fit a decent-sized system.”

The transition from decision to generation was remarkably swift. The installation took just five days: one day to erect the scaffolding, three days of technical work, and a final day to pack up and leave.

The aesthetic impact was also a pleasant surprise. “They're all installed at the back of the property, so they are completely invisible from the front of the house,” says Julia. “They just look incredibly neat and tidy.”

However, the most satisfying shift has been financial. “Our energy bills have actually gone into credit,” Julia says. “We are currently selling far more electricity back to the grid than we are actually using.”

Smarter storage, lower bills

Pairing their solar panels with a battery allows the Rockwells to automatically store low-cost energy and power their heat pump seamlessly ( Octopus Energy )

The true game-changer for the Rockwells was pairing their 17 panels with a Tesla Powerwall battery, which has completely transformed how they think about household energy.

“Because we have a heat pump installed, we’re on the Cosy Octopus tariff,” Julia explains. “That gives us three hours of super-cheap electricity in the afternoon, a couple of hours from 10pm, and another three hours in the early hours of the morning. We now time our washing machine and dishwasher to run during those windows.”

The smart tech does the heavy lifting for them. “The Tesla battery is incredibly clever. It automatically charges itself up from the grid when the tariff is at its cheapest, meaning we can draw from that stored, low-cost power when grid prices spike during the day.”

For the Rockwells, the beauty of this integrated system is its absolute simplicity. “We don’t have to micro-manage it at all,” Julia says. “We just sit back, look outside at the sunshine, and know we're making money.”

Driving on rays

Generating so much excess power inspired the couple to switch to electric vehicles, running both their home and transport on clean energy ( Octopus Energy )

The financial rewards have been rapid. In their first six months alone, the system generated more than £300 worth of electricity – prompting the couple to take the final step in their green transition. “Because we were generating so much excess power, we decided to switch to electric cars,” Julia says. “Now, our home and our transport are totally electric.”

Looking back, Julia has no regrets and strongly encourages others to look past the initial hesitation.

“If you are looking for a way to keep your long-term energy costs low, and you have savings sitting in a bank account earning virtually nothing, it is an incredibly smart investment,” she says. “Plus, it’s bound to add value to the property. Any future buyer will see the system is already up, running, and saving money – so if we ever do decide to sell, we’ll reap the rewards of that, too.”

Five water-dropping planes and another five helicopters took off at first light Monday to help hundreds of firefighters battling a major wildfire west of Athens, Greece, a day after a midair collision between two firefighting helicopters killed two crew members.

The collision laid bare the danger at the most volatile front of Europe’s wildfire emergency. Flames bore down deeper into the region of the Greek capital, forcing fresh evacuations in the early hours of Monday. In France, firefighters guarded a still-burning scar four times the size of Paris.

The two crew members — one Greek and one Danish national — died when their helicopter collided with another near the seaside area of Psatha while tackling the fire that started Friday morning. The blaze raged through pine forests and scrubland through the weekend, whipped by gale force winds that often prevented water-dropping planes from operating.

The crew of the second helicopter – a Greek and a British national – were taken to a hospital, where their injuries were reported to be light. Foreign firefighting and helicopter crews are often deployed in Greece to help tackle wildfires during the country’s hot, dry summers.

Easing winds raise hopes of halting the advance of the flames

Strong winds were dying down Monday, raising hopes that the nearly 500 firefighters battling the blaze could manage to halt its advance. But authorities warned the broader Athens region of Attica remained at a high risk for wildfires due to a forecast increase in temperatures.

More than 1,000 people have been evacuated from the region, including more than 250 rescued by boats from beaches in the area. Evacuation orders were issued in the early hours of Monday for three more areas, while crews worked to create firebreaks in a forest to help halt the advance of the blaze.

Greece’s firefighting department said Sunday the fire apparently began from sparks emitted by a faulty power line transporting electricity from a private wind generator facility to the main electricity network.

Two people were arrested — an electrical engineer responsible for designing and overseeing the power project, and a contractor involved in constructing the electricity transmission network. Both face felony arson charges, while authorities had also issued an arrest warrant for the owner of the wind generator company.

Greece has devastating wildfires every summer, with hot, dry conditions and frequently strong winds making it easy for small sparks to trigger major blazes. Measures to limit fire risks, such as bans on barbecues and certain outdoor work such as welding and use of electrical power saws are often ignored. The vast majority of the hundreds of wildfires the country has each year are caused by negligence.

But some fires are deliberately set. On Sunday, authorities said one man was arrested on Kefalonia on suspicion of having started a fire that spread quickly in the southeastern part of the island, triggering the evacuation of nearby villages.

Major blaze in France contained, but hotspots remain

Farther west, France’s largest wildfire remained held within its perimeter on Sunday night after forcing 224,000 people to flee in what may have been the country’s largest civilian evacuation outside wartime.

Hot spots still burned within a 420-square-kilometer (162-square-mile) scar, thousands remained unable to return home, and nearly 3,000 firefighters were deployed against the Gironde megafire and a second blaze in Provence.

Together, fires in France and Spain have driven roughly a third of a million people from homes and vacation sites, emptied communities at the height of the European summer and stretched emergency services across simultaneous disasters.

___

Adamson reported from Paris.

Indonesian rescuers were searching for possible missing passengers Monday after rescuing 229 people from a ferry that caught fire the previous day in waters off the main island of Java, leaving at least five people dead.

The Mutiara Sentosa 2 ferry was traveling from Indonesia’s second-largest city of Surabaya in East Java to the city of Makassar in South Sulawesi, and initial reports said it was carrying 232 passengers and 39 crew members, based on the ship’s manifest, when the fire broke out between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. in waters off Sumenep regency.

However, by Monday morning officials said many more people were aboard than listed, and that the number of people still missing was unclear after 229 people were rescued and five bodies recovered. Officials are relying on reports from the families of victims and survivors in an attempt to determine the number of those missing.

It is common in Indonesia for the number of passengers on a boat or ferry to differ from the manifest. Such discrepancies can reflect overcrowding and complicate search and rescue efforts, said Nanang Sigit, who heads the Surabaya Search and Rescue Office.

The cause of the fire was not immediately known and remained under investigation.

The vessel was also loaded with 180 vehicles, mostly trucks, and an excavator.

Ahmad Abdul Karim, one of the survivors, said the fire appeared to have started from a truck on the lower vehicle deck.

“Fanned by the wind, the flames spread extremely quickly," Karim said, "In less than 30 minutes, everyone had been instructed to move to the bow of the ferry.”

Search and rescue teams dispatched a rescue boat from Surabaya to the scene, about 35 kilometers (22 miles) north of Buruan Sapudi island in the Sumenep regency. Indonesian navy ships also assisted along with a number of passing vessels near the location of the incident.

The ferry was built in Japan in 1992 and operated there before being sold to Indonesia in 2015. With a length of 160 meters (525 feet), it can accommodate 689 passengers and 49 crew, along with up to 181 vehicles.

The Mutiara Sentosa 2 serves the Surabaya-Makassar route, a voyage that typically takes around 40 hours and is primarily used by domestic travelers and cargo transport between the islands of Java and Sulawesi.

Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands where ferries are a common method of travel. Disasters occur regularly, with weak safety enforcement often blamed.

___

Associated Press journalists Niniek Karmini and Edna Tarigan in Jakarta, Indonesia, contributed to this report.

News.title: Inside the trial for an experimental malaria vaccine
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Careless Liverpool throw away 2-0 lead in pre-season defeat by Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Massage guns vs compression boots: Which is better for muscle recovery?
News.content:
Looking after your body is no longer just about getting a good workout in; it’s ensuring that you’re properly recuperating afterwards, too. Luckily, in 2026, there is a huge range of products designed to aid recovery.

In fact, the recovery tech boom is playing a big role in the growth of the sports technology market overall. Estimates show it’s projected to grow from $39.6 billion in 2026 to $192.3 billion by 2034.

Two of the most popular products in this category are massage guns and compression boots. Both claim to ease muscle soreness and help you bounce back to training sooner, but they sit at very different price points. You can pick up a basic gun from around £40, whereas the cheapest boots we tested were £300. But which method is actually better for improving workout recovery?

Massage guns can help to improve flexibility in older muscles

Massage guns work by delivering repeated percussion and vibration to one specific area, which helps improve the mobility and flexibility of a specific muscle. In turn, this can make your muscles feel less tense and stiff. These gadgets can be used before and after workout sessions.

While useful for all ages, massage guns can be helpful for anyone looking to improve range of movement, ease muscle stiffness and boost blood flow – whether exercising or not.

“It will help temporarily improve your mobility so that you feel like you’ve got a bit more flexibility in that muscle,” explains Jonathan Wreaves, clinical physiologist at preventative health clinic Viavi.

But how do they actually work?

Most massage guns offer a revolutions per minute (RPM) range, which refers to how many times the massage head moves back and forth every minute. This tends to be somewhere between 1200 and 3500. The lower range is ideal for gentle massage and warming up, while a higher RPM is better for targeting bigger muscle groups and more intense tightness.

Sports.title: Unseen footage shows how Argentina got Falklands flag as fan unintentionally films World Cup security breach
Sports.content:
NEW footage has emerged showing how Argentina’s controversial Falklands flag got onto the pitch moments after their victory over England.

Lionel Messi and Co broke the Three Lions’ hearts with a late 2-1 victory in Atlanta.



After the match, Argentina stars caused uproar by posing with a flag that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas” – meaning The Falklands are Argentine” in English.

Premier League stars Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez were both seen holding the flag up alongside ex-Tottenham midfielder Giovani Lo Celso.



Social media user Clara Houssay attended the match.

And more than a fortnight on, she realised that she had captured the moment that the flag made its way onto the turf on video.

Her clip clearly features the banner being lobbed down from the mob of joyous Argentine fans.

Lo Celso is the player that can be seen running over to grab it, before some of his team-mates join in.

Argentina’s flag provoked fury in England given the 1982 conflict over the islands that cost hundreds of lives, and that inhabitants have since voted overwhelmingly to remain British.

Hothead midfielder Leandro Paredes subsequently doubled down, claiming that the Falklands “will always be Argentine”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Goalkeeper Emi Martinez praised his team-mates for “playing with a knife between their teeth” and added that England stars “didn’t feel the same way”.

But quizzed if the Falklands conflict had played its part in their motivation, Martinez was not convinced.

He is quoted as saying, in his native Spanish, “I don’t think it’s because of that. It’s in the past. I wasn’t even born.”

Fifa last month opened a disciplinary investigation against Argentina for the flag, as well as for their players’ reactions to losing the final to Spain.



Rules ban players from “using a sports event for ­demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

In 2014, Argentina were hit with a £20,000 fine for holding up a banner with a similar Falklands message before a match against Slovenia.

Flags referencing the Falklands were banned from the stadium by Fifa ahead of the match.

But security did not spot the message, which was written on a hotel sheet, when the Argentina fan entered the stadium.

And it was Lo Celso, rather than the stadium stewards, who was first to the object once it was launched onto the pitch.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces FIFA revolt as furious colleagues demand he quits over ‘shabby’ World Cup sell-off deal
Sports.content:
SHAMED Gianni Infantino was clinging to power last night as it emerged Fifa is expected to hold an emergency meeting to oust him over his plan to sell off the World Cup.

The £4.3 million-a-year boss is likely to be asked to step down at a council meeting after he finally bowed to pressure and axed his “shabby, backroom deal”.



And if he refuses to resign, then another candidate with the backing of his opponents would be put up to challenge him in next year’s spring presidential election.

One senior football source told The Sunday Times: “Infantino had it all and his reckless greed means he has now lost it. He’s an embarrassment and he’s not a lame duck, but a dead duck.”



The wave of negative publicity around the disgraced fatcat’s plan to flog off stakes in the World Cup to private investors has reportedly seen sponsors contacting Fifa in panic.

And even bank JP Morgan, which was heavily involved in the project, allegedly wants out.



Fifa was reportedly already planning to force an extraordinary general meeting before Infantino’s £15 billion “secret scheme” emerged last week.

Council members are said to have demanded an independent review into the tycoon’s unprecedented decision to lift US star Folarin Balogun’s red card during the World Cup after taking calls from Donald Trump.

The assembly could now develop into a full blown leadership challenge.

It is also possible that 41 of Fifa’s 211 member nations could call an emergency congress and stage a vote of no confidence in the shamed leader.



Potential challengers for the top job include current Concacaf president Victor Montagliani, Asian football chief Sheikh Salman, or Paris Saint-Germain boss Nasser Al Khelaifi.

Sources close to Montagliani believe he may already have 96 votes – from UEFA and Concacaf – if he challenges Infantino.

The Swiss’ plans, which involved selling 20 per cent of a new World Cup operating company to an investment firm owned by the younger brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, sparked international outrage.

Furious football chiefs and politicians have called for him to fall on his sword.



European football’s governing body Uefa accused the magnate of trying to “sell off the family silver”. It said his “shabby, backroom deal” had “lost Uefa’s confidence” and that of the wider football family.

The North and Central American Football Association Concacaf said he had “stopped putting football first” and called for a “comprehensive reckoning with this presidency”.

And on Saturday evening, Javier Tebas, president of Spain’s LaLiga, declared Infantino’s “time is up” and demanded that “world football needs new leadership”.

England great Peter Reid, 70, also joined calls for the Fifa chief to step down.



The Everton legend told The Sunday Mirror: “Infantino’s position is untenable now, people have lost faith in him…Private investors in football – that is just wrong.

“Fifa has hundreds of millions already, they should be putting more money into grassroots. That is where the money should go, instead of getting into bed with private investors.”

Infantino has so far only received backing from the associations of Qatar, Morocco and Lebanon.

Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup and Morocco is vying to host the final in 2030.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



The Fifa president’s u-turn in the early hours of Saturday morning came after his right-hand man Carlos Coderio quit in disgust and chief operating officer Kevin Lamour announced staff had been “deceived”.

But he refused to give in to mounting pressure to resign, insisting that his intent in the coming days is “to bring all interested parties back together…in the spirit of shared interest in our game”.

Smicer, who won the Champions League with the Reds in 2005, believes Iraola's relationship with Scott, with the Basque previously coaching Scott on the South Coast, could sweeten a deal should Liverpool move for the player.

"I think you can expect Andoni Iraola would like to take Alex Scott because he knows what he can do," Smicer said, via Casinostugan.

"To be honest, in midfield we need a bit more spark with people who are fighting but are clever going forward, turning quickly with the ball and finding strikers. Of course, we expect a lot from (Florian) Wirtz to do this. But Andoni Iraola knows Alex Scott. If the price is right and he sees the possibility to strengthen the team, why not?

‌



View 3 Images Alex Scott starred for Bournemouth last season (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

"Curtis Jones is linked with a few moves, and if he leaves, we need midfield press. We don't know what's happening with (Alexis) Mac Allister, he had a bit of a weak season and was not at the same level. (Ryan) Gravenberch had a good start, but then it was not the best. Only (Dominik) Szoboszlai was a top player in midfield for the whole season.

"In midfield you need competition, and Scott can be a great asset because he's only twenty-two and is playing regularly for the England youth teams. He's a good prospect and a local guy from the UK.

Article continues below

"These things are important. I don't know if he would love to play for Liverpool, but not many players would turn them down. He's got a good chance now because Andoni Iraola is the new manager. If he likes him, I think we can find the money."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly transfer boost as medical booked and star 'says yes' to move
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly transfer boost as medical booked and star 'says yes' to move

Manchester United are enjoying an under-the-radar transfer window as they continue to target a handful of positions

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is enjoying his first pre-season as Manchester United manager (Image: Getty)

Manchester United are one game closer to the new Premier League season. And Michael Carrick's squad has so far only been bolstered by three new senior arrivals.

‌



United fans were made to wait for their club to spring into action this window but were rewarded by a flurry of incomings. Andrey Santos was quickly followed by ex-Leeds United goalkeeper Karl Darlow and Youri Tielemans through the door. Young prospects in Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson were also snapped up.

‌



Their latest pre-season outing saw them defeat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in Stockholm. But one position that the club are keen to reinforce is left-back. Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui can operate there, but a surprise move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly has been mooted.

‌



United have long held an interest in the defender and another transfer that might be completed this week could enable Carrick's side to pounce. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer news out of Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Myles Lewis-Skelly boost

United were first linked with Lewis-Skelly last year when he found himself falling down the left-back pecking order at Arsenal. Both Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie were getting more minutes.

‌



View 3 Images Lewis-Skelly was a Premier League title winner last season (Image: Getty)

This was soon resolved when Mikel Arteta moved the 19-year-old into midfield and he impressed. However, Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes is set for a Gunners medical on Monday, according to The Times. If the Brazilian does sign, he'll become one more star Lewis-Skelly has to compete with for first-team minutes. Not to mention, his reported £80m transfer sum will leave a dent.

Any fee Arsenal get from selling Lewis-Skelly would be pure profit when taking into account Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, so if United lodge the right offer, it could be too good to turn down.

‌



The Independent reports that they are currently waiting to see whether the Gunners are open to doing business regarding Lewis-Skelly and that United's interest remains strong.

Man Utd star 'agrees' to move

On the outgoings front, reports from Italy suggest Joshua Zirkzee has agreed to join Juventus on loan with no obligation to buy. The Dutch forward does not appear to be part of Carrick's first-team plans.

View 3 Images Zirkzee has reportedly agreed to join Juventus (Image: Getty)

‌



United bought Zirkzee for £36m in 2024 and he became the first signing under the ownership of INEOS. He previously played in Italy with Bologna.

It is understood that Zirkzee has become a difficult player to sell and, having not been able to cut it at United, is far more likely to head out on loan, either with or without an option to buy.

La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee has agreed to such a deal with Juventus and has already 'said yes' to the Italian outfit. However, the move is hinging on the Old Lady being able to offload striker Jonathan David.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Real Madrid issue Vinicius Jr update as Mikel Arteta drops transfer hint
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Real Madrid issue Vinicius Jr update as Mikel Arteta drops transfer hint

It's shaping up to be a blockbuster final month of the transfer window for Arsenal, who have their eye on several high-profile transfers

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has some good news for Arsenal fans (Image: Getty Images)

It's been something of a slow summer for Arsenal in the transfer market - but that could be about to change. The Gunners have taken a measured approach to their business so far, with Christos Tzolis their only major arrival after completing a £34million deal to sign the Greek winger from Club Brugge last month.

‌



Piero Hincapie's loan switch from Bayer Leverkusen has also been made permanent after Arsenal triggered the defender's £34.5m buy clause, while goalkeeper Illan Meslier arrived on a free transfer following the expiry of his Leeds contract. Even so, Mikel Arteta's side are still waiting to make the kind of statement signing many supporters expected ahead of their first Premier League title defence in more than 20 years.

‌



That could soon change. Arsenal are in advanced talks over a move for Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes and continue to be heavily linked with a blockbuster swoop for Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr - a prospect that has understandably sent excitement levels soaring among the Emirates faithful.

‌



But as talks continue behind the scenes, fresh developments have emerged. With that in mind, here are the latest Arsenal-related transfer headlines.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal forced to release short statement after Christos Tzolis debut READ MORE :

Real Madrid issue Vinicius Jr update

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has confirmed that Vinicius Jr will return to training with the rest of the squad on Monday despite the uncertainty surrounding his future.

‌



The Brazilian forward remains locked in a contract stand-off with the Spanish giants and, with less than 12 months remaining on his current deal, pressure is continuing to build on both sides.

Arsenal are closely monitoring the situation and are ready to offer Vinicius Jr a route out of the Bernabeu should talks collapse. However, the 26-year-old does not appear set to take any drastic action to force a move.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is out of contract next summer and Arsenal are looking to take advantage (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"On Monday, Vini Jr, Brahim, and Bernardo will arrive," Mourinho told Real Madrid's official website. "I'm concerned about not having everyone, and I would like to have three weeks of work with the others. It's not possible."

Talks over a new contract remain ongoing, with both parties still hoping to reach an agreement. However, negotiations appear to be at an impasse and if the deadlock continues, Arsenal will be ready to pounce.

Arteta drops major transfer hint

Mikel Arteta has hinted that Arsenal are preparing for a busy end to the transfer window, revealing the club have "very ambitious" plans and telling supporters to "expect movements" over the coming weeks.

‌



The Gunners have been slow out of the blocks in the transfer market this summer, with the rest of the 'Big Six' spending nearly £850m between them on new players. But that looks set to change, with Arteta insisting that the club will not "sit still" for much longer.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta has suggested that Arsenal will be busy in the transfer market in the coming weeks (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"We are already active and trying to improve on and evolve the team. That is clear," he said. "We expect to have movements in the next few weeks. Obviously we want to get better like anyone else and you can see the transfer market, and our opponents, what we are doing. We won't sit still and we are very ambitious with where we want to go."

‌



Arteta refused to be drawn on reports linking Arsenal with a sensational move for Vinicius Jr, instead responding with a wry smile and a simple "thank you" when asked about the Real Madrid forward.

The Spaniard also stressed the importance of strengthening his squad to raise standards across the board, explaining that Arsenal are looking to add greater competition for places while addressing any remaining weaknesses before the new campaign begins.

"The margins are very small, we want to get better and the level is going to increase," he said. "We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don’t have in the team, to have bigger margins. That's the way we have to think."

Sports.title: Pressure grows on FIFA chief Infantino to resign as FA member pulls support
Sports.content:
Pressure grows on FIFA chief Infantino to resign as FA member pulls support

A football association from the UK has become the first to officially withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election next March, days after he U-turned on plans to 'sell off' the World Cup

View 3 Images Infantino is under pressure (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

A British football association has become the first FIFA member to officially pull its support for Gianni Infantino's re-election.

‌



The move is set to heap pressure on the Italian, who faces a severe backlash over his plans 'sell off' the World Cup. Even after cancelling the project, set to be led by a close Donald Trump ally, the FIFA President is rapidly losing support from major players in the game.

‌



The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has now reportedly made its position clear and written to FIFA to withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election.

‌



The FAW also backed a boycott of FIFA competitions orchestrated by European governing body, UEFA, in response to Infantino's plan to create a private company, open to investment, to run its headline competitions to raise billions of pounds.

It was reportedly going to be led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law. After Infantino’s plans were revealed by the media, before some high-ranking FIFA officials were even informed of his intentions, he faced a severe backlash.

UEFA, the organisation which runs European football, said it would boycott FIFA competitions until the plans were killed, and CONCACAF, its North American counterpart, also criticised the plans. Key advisers to Infantino also resigned in protest.

‌



View 3 Images Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Italian Infantino is due for re-election in March, but his future at the top of world football looks in doubt after this latest scandal.

Now, the FAW has heaped pressure on his tenure, officially withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election, according to reports.

‌



The association told Sky News it "hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027-2031 term.

"The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football.

View 3 Images Wales failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, but did appear at Qatar 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

"Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.

“The Football Association of Wales has written to FIFA to inform them of their position.”

Other British football associations are yet to follow suit, but all approved the UEFA boycott. However, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has gone one step further and said Infantino is ‘the wrong man’ to lead FIFA.

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-4 LEEDS UNITED: Daniel Farke's men scored four goals in 25 second-half minutes to stun the Reds and win in the Premier League Summer Series on Sunday

View 3 Images Leeds United beat Liverpool 4-2 on Sunday as they mounted a stunning comeback (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool were left stunned as Leeds United produced a scintillating second-half comeback to come from 2-0 down and beat the Reds 4-2 in the Premier League Super Series.

‌



Fresh off the back of beating Sunderland and Championship side Wrexham, Andoni Iraola's side started on the front foot against Leeds and opened the scoring inside the first seven minutes. Luke Chambers was the goalscorer for the Reds as he smashed home from close range.

‌



Although Leeds did have some opportunities, Liverpool controlled most of the first half and ended up doubling their advantage just before the break. Florian Wirtz found the net for Iraola's side, as he finished off an excellent team move, tucking the ball home into the corner.

‌



Both teams made four substitutions at half-time and it was Leeds who came out as the stronger after the break. Brendan Aaronson capitalised on a mistake to pull one back for Daniel Farke's side on the hour mark, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised with a finish from inside the box.

The comeback was then complete soon after with Sean Longstaff firing home following some neat play from Aaronson. Calvert-Lewin added his second and Leeds' fourth late on to ensure the Whites were crowned as the winners of the 2026 Premier League Summer Series in the United States.

Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Mirror Football looks at the big talking points from the game...

‌



Fast Liverpool start

Liverpool scored the first goal in each of their first two pre-season friendlies and that theme continued against Leeds. Chambers, who has come into central defence since Joe Gomez suffered a new muscle injury in the 4-2 win over Sunderland last week, was the man who gave the Reds the lead.

Dominik Szoboszlai's outswinging corner was flicked on by Milos Kerkez and Chambers was there free inside the box to slam home from eight yards. In truth, it was a smart finish from the 22-year-old, who could have easily got underneath the ball but he kept his head over it before lashing beyond goalkeeper Alex Cairns.

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz scored for Liverpool against Leeds (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Huge Leeds injury blow

One of Daniel Farke's main wishes going into the fixture against Liverpool would have been to avoid any fresh injuries with three weeks to go until the start of the Premier League season. Well, unfortunately for him and the Whites Gabriel Gudmundsson hobbled off with what looked like a hamstring problem.

After going down in the opening stages with a knock, Gudmundsson carried on before being substituted in the 34th minute. The Sweden international went down appearing to hold his hamstring and was treated by the Leeds medical staff before going off and being replaced by Sebastiaan Bornauw.

Impressive Wirtz

Following a mixed first season and Liverpool's lack of attacking transfer business so far this summer, it does feel as though there is some pressure on Wirtz to produce in 2026/27. But the German showed in his first appearance back after the World Cup that he can step up and deliver after scoring the Reds' second against Leeds.

‌



It was well-worked move by Liverpool as Trey Nyoni's cross-field pass found Jeremie Frimpong who cut the ball back for Wirtz to sweep home first time from inside the box. With just seven goals in 49 matches in his debut season at the Reds, Wirtz will be no doubt wanting to improve on that total this term.

View 3 Images Wirtz had an impressive first-half

Liverpool punished for mistake

Although it's much better to iron out mistakes in pre-season, of course, Liverpool won't want to give too many goals like the one Leeds scored against them in Chicago.

‌



Milos Kerkez, who endured a difficult first season at the Reds following his move from Bournemouth last summer, gave the ball away inside his own half and Leeds punished them. Ampadu collected the ball and drove at the Liverpool back-line before playing in Aaronson and he slotted low past Giorgi Mamardashvili. It was a slack piece of play from Kerkez and he must eradicate them if he wants to be a success at Anfield.

Impressive comeback from Leeds

Leeds were much-improved after Calvert-Lewin, Aaronson, Sean Longstaff and Harry Wilson came on at half-time and they produced a scintillating comeback to stun Liverpool.

After Aaronson pulled one back, Calvert-Lewin levelled for the Whites in the 71st minute. A long-throw from Ampadu caused chaos in the box and Joe Rodon's flick-on was hammered home by Calvert-Lewin from close-range.

‌



Then, just two minutes later, the fightback was complete as Leeds took the lead for the first time in the game. Longstaff was the scorer on this occasion for Leeds, as he swivelled inside the area before drilling home.

The Whites would go on to score a fourth goal to seal the win and it came from another long throw. This time it was Bornauw who got the flick on and Calvert-Lewin was there once more to tap home from four yards.

It was an impressive comeback from Leeds and excellent character after falling 2-0 down and looking like the game was over at half-time. But Farke has instilled some belief into his side and it was on show in full flow again.

‌



Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer priorities clear

If it wasn't clear before that Liverpool need to sign some players, it certainly is now. The Reds have got to bring in at least two, if not, three ready-made first-team starters before their Premier League opener against Newcastle United.

They have been among the quietest clubs in the top flight when it comes to signing players this summer and it's seen Iraola's squad look threadbare with Ibrahima Konate, Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah moving on. Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz have come in, but neither have made an appearance for the Reds so far.

The Reds are so light in a number of areas and the one that looked the weakest against Leeds was the centre-back area. While Jacquet is coming in to join Virgil van Dijk and the returning Giovani Leoni, Gomez's latest injury blow should see Iraola's side dip into the market to sign another central defender. That is a must.

Article continues below

As well as that, the Reds are lacking a serious right winger following Salah's departure, while it does still feel like they need a new left-back to help Kerkez and a high-profile central midfielder.

Sports.title: UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'
Sports.content:
UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'

UEFA are reported to have sent a letter to FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, as the aftermath of the failed FFE plans continue

View 2 Images UEFA havei issued a legal threat to FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

UEFA have threatened under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino with legal action - and warned him against destroying any documents relating to the failed World Cup ‘sale’ plan.

‌



Controversial news emerged earlier this week that FIFA had plans to sell shares in the organisation's tournaments, which would have included the men’s and women’s World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup. The plans were met with widespread criticism, with UEFA being joined by CONCACAF and AFC in making it clear they were against such plans, which were going to be called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

‌



UEFA, following a meeting with its 55 member associations, threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions if the proposals put forward by the governing body and Infantino went ahead. The backlash eventually led to Infantino releasing a statement which confirmed the controversial scheme was to be scrapped, citing the ‘division’ within football as a reason.

‌



5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

The Telegraph has now claimed to have seen a letter which has been sent by UEFA to FIFA, as well as potential investors Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, JP Morgan and OpenEconomics. It has been reported that UEFA has threatened legal action and has warned FIFA not to destroy any evidence relating to the failed FFE proposals.

“Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below,” a letter written by UEFA and seen by the Telegraph, says.

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

‌



“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino was forced to perform a dramatic u-turn with the FFE proposals (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The letter continued: “Uefa – as well as other confederations, Fifa member associations and football stakeholders – has strongly condemned the FFE plan in the strongest terms as fundamentally incompatible with the proper governance of football.

“Given that proceedings are reasonably anticipated, you are obliged to preserve all relevant materials (as defined below) with immediate effect.”

In another warning to FIFA, UEFA are quoted as adding in the letter: “Uefa puts you on formal notice that any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice – or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated – may constitute spoliation of evidence.

Article continues below

“Uefa reserves all rights to seek appropriate remedies in the proceedings for any such destruction or loss, including applications for adverse inference orders, sanctions, and costs against the responsible party or parties.”
