World.title: Center Party leader backs temporary border controls over migration concerns
World.content:
Center Party chair Mihhail Kõlvart backs temporarily restoring border controls in the Schengen area, saying Estonia must also prioritize security over free movement slogans.

In a social media post on Saturday, Kõlvart pointed to Spain's Ceuta migration crisis as a warning of how quickly border pressures can escalate. He said decisions by authorities and courts had contributed to a situation where tens of thousands of people entered Europe within a short period.

"We can speculate about how much of this happened unintentionally and to what extent someone from the outside deliberately contributed to it, but in any case, it showed how easily such a crisis can emerge and escalate," he said, adding that migration pressure has also been used as a hybrid tactic against Europe.

Kõlvart said these recent events also serve as a reminder that in a crisis, every country must first look after its own interests. He cited Italy's temporary restoration of border controls with Spain as an example.

"Estonia, too, must also put its own interests first and prioritize its own security," he stressed.

The opposition party chair criticized Prime Minister Kristen Michal's (Reform) recent statement that free movement in Europe is a top priority and that temporarily reinstating Schengen border controls is not in Estonia's interests, calling the stance a slogan disconnected from reality.

"Free movement does not outweigh the need to mitigate the security threats Europe is currently facing," Kõlvart said.

'Estonia isn't prepared for this'

He also dismissed the prime minister's calls to hold those organizing the migration accountable as just rhetoric, saying things have already spiraled out of control and the damage has already been done in Spain.

"Unfortunately, we have to acknowledge that Estonia currently isn't prepared for migration crises like this either," Kõlvart said, warning that even a crisis a fraction of that size would be catastrophic for Estonia.

"This does not mean that everyone should fend for themselves in difficult times or that no one should help an EU member state in need," he continued. "Of course we must help Spain, but Spain itself must also take appropriate steps toward resolving this crisis, and take steps to prevent it from happening again."

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform). Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Kõlvart said the issue cannot be addressed by allowing problems to spread across Europe. While acknowledging that many migrants who arrived in Spain have since left, he said guarantees are needed that further migration waves will not follow.

"Until then, temporarily restoring border controls is a necessary and justified step," he concluded.

PM supports Spain, rejects border controls

Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco this week. As of Friday evening, more than 48,000 people had voluntarily returned to Morocco, Spanish officials said.

The influx comes after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla, another Spanish enclave, cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

Michal signed a joint letter with 21 other member states addressed to the EU's top leaders on Saturday calling for "an immediate and coordinated European response."

Responding to comments from opposition Isamaa chair Urmas Reinsalu, the prime minister also pushed back on the suggestion that suspending free movement within the EU's Schengen area would be justified in such a critical situation.

Calling the Schengen area a "great value," Michal wrote on social media that establishing new internal borders within it is in no way in Estonia's interests.

"None of us wants to return to a time when traveling overland to Central Europe meant passing through more than five cumbersome border checks," he said.

World.title: Gallery: Setos elect new leader at one-day Seto Kingdom
World.content:
Thousands gathered in Mikitamäe for Seto Kingdom Day on Saturday, where local culture advocate Ingrit Kala was elected the next ülembsootska, or leader of the Seto people.

Now in its 33rd year, the annual Seto Kingdom Day in Southeastern Estonia returned to Mikitamäe on Saturday, where sprawling grounds at the heart of the village were packed with celebrations, contests and showcases of the Seto language, food, culture, history and people.

The event culminated with the direct election of a new ülembsootska, chief regent of the Seto god-king Peko and ceremonial leader of the Seto people.

Thousands of people took part, lining up in front of their preferred candidate and gripping a rope extending from each to cast their vote.

Kala defeated fellow candidate and former nuursootska, or youth regent, Rain Oper, by a margin of several hundred supporters.

Succeeding Jalmar Vabarna, Kala will be joined in her role as leader of the Setos for the year by returning nuursootska Maria Grünberg, who was elected by children and teens the day before.

The 33rd Seto Kingdom Day took place in Mikitamäe on Saturday. August 1, 2026. Source: Leevi Lillemäe/ERR

"You have to be there for your own people, of course, and when you are invited somewhere, you go and bring them your blessing," said Kala, noting that it's important to work beyond the Seto community as well, to boost their visibility.

Kala added that developing and preserving the local Seto language would be one of her priorities as ülembsootska, noting that fewer people speak it today.

"Especially for young people, so that the Seto language doesn't disappear completely," she emphasized.

'There's always something'

Local resident Signe said Seto Kingdom Day brings together not just Setos, but those who feel connected to the Seto identity as well.

"I haven't lived here long — this is now my second year living in Setomaa," she said, adding that she had followed her heart to the region.

For Signe, one of the most important parts of the annual celebration is that it brings people together, reconnecting familiar faces and giving them a chance to catch up.

"There's always something," she added. "It's the little things that make it a wonderful day."

World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: Iraq, NATO agree to open mission office in Baghdad, expand security cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews,com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi and the commander of the NATO Mission Iraq (NMI), Lt. Gen. Ramon Armada, agreed on Sunday to open a NATO mission office in Baghdad while reaffirming continued cooperation on military training, cybersecurity, and strategic security partnerships.

According to a statement from al-Aboudi’s media office, cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the two officials held talks via video conference to discuss regional security developments and NATO’s ongoing support for Iraq’s armed forces.

During the discussion, both sides stressed the importance of reducing regional tensions and resolving recurring crises through dialogue and diplomatic channels. They also reviewed mechanisms for continuing NATO assistance in the areas of military training, advisory support, intelligence sharing, and capacity building.

A key outcome of the meeting was an agreement to establish a NATO Mission office in Baghdad, further strengthening coordination between the alliance and Iraqi security institutions.

Al-Aboudi said NATO’s role in Iraq remains focused on non-combat activities, including military advisory services, training, capacity building, cybersecurity support, and cooperation in artificial intelligence. He added that Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government is pursuing a policy of engagement with friendly and neighboring countries to advance development, investment, and mutually beneficial partnerships.

For his part, Armada reaffirmed that NATO’s advisory and training mission is committed to helping develop the capabilities of Iraq’s armed forces to address future security challenges. He said the alliance remains committed to supporting Iraq in line with the priorities established by the Iraqi government.

World.title: Zaidi threatens to resign as Coordination Framework divided over response to Saudi strikes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly threatened to resign during a recent meeting of the Coordination Framework amid deep divisions over how Iraq should respond to recent Saudi military strikes, according to a report published Sunday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada.

Citing political sources, the newspaper said the prime minister’s remarks came during a tense meeting that exposed growing disagreements among senior Shiite leaders over security policy, the role of armed factions, and Baghdad’s handling of escalating regional tensions.

According to the report, the meeting became increasingly heated after intelligence was presented alleging that the armed group Saraya Awliya al-Dam was preparing to launch an attack against Jordan from Iraqi territory. The sources said Amman had warned Baghdad it would respond to any attack originating from Iraq, further intensifying the debate.

The report claims the dispute centered on whether Iraq should adhere to the government’s official position or allow individual armed factions to respond independently to the recent Saudi strikes. While most Coordination Framework leaders reportedly backed the government’s approach, one influential figure with ties to Saraya Awliya al-Dam insisted on carrying out a unilateral response.

Al-Mada reported that armed factions have given the government until next Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia. According to the sources, they warned that if Baghdad fails to act, they may launch their own response.

The newspaper also reported that the escalating dispute prompted al-Zaidi to again raise the possibility of resigning, marking what would be the second time he has reportedly made such a threat since taking office. According to the report, he previously suggested stepping down if his anti-corruption agenda failed.

The sources further claimed that the prime minister is facing mounting political pressure, including concerns about his personal security, although no official statements have confirmed those assertions.

The report also focused on the investigation into drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, stating that seven Iraqi-Saudi security meetings, with U.S. participation in some sessions, have been held over the past two months.

According to Al-Mada’s sources, the investigations have not produced conclusive evidence proving that the attacks originated from Iraqi territory, despite Saudi accusations.

The report said several scenarios remain under discussion, including the possibility that Iraqi armed factions were responsible, that Houthi operatives present in Iraq facilitated the attacks, or alternative theories promoted by some factions alleging Israeli activity in Iraq’s southern desert regions.

According to the newspaper, the ongoing crisis led al-Zaidi to cancel a planned visit to Saudi Arabia, which Iraqi officials reportedly viewed as an opportunity to attract much-needed Saudi investment at a time when Iraq faces mounting financial pressures.

The report also said armed factions have urged the prime minister to suspend efforts to bring all weapons under state control, arguing that the recent Saudi strikes have fundamentally altered the security landscape.

Al-Mada also reported that discussions during the meeting touched on the role of Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Faleh al-Fayyadh during the recent U.S.-Saudi strikes that targeted PMF facilities.

According to the newspaper’s sources, claims circulated that al-Zaidi had warned al-Fayyadh upon returning from Turkey that PMF sites could be targeted, and that evacuation efforts were delayed. However, other participants reportedly dismissed those claims, suggesting they reflected internal political disputes rather than established facts.

The Iraqi government has previously denied having prior knowledge of the U.S.-Saudi strikes. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad neither approved nor was informed in advance of the attacks.

However, U.S. President Donald Trump later told Fox News that the strikes had been coordinated with the Iraqi government, presenting an account that differs from Baghdad’s official position.

World.title: Zaidi’s failed raid on Nujaba base exposes challenges in disarmament push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A failed security operation targeting a facility belonging to the Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba movement has underscored the challenges facing the Iraqi government as it seeks to bring all armed groups under state control before the end of September.

According to a report published by Al-Monitor, a joint Iraqi force attempted to search a Harakat al-Nujaba compound in Baghdad’s Jurf al-Naddaf district on July 24 after receiving intelligence suggesting the site contained missiles and drones. However, the operation ended without the facility being searched after armed members of the group confronted government forces.

The report, citing Iraqi security officials, said the operation involved Baghdad Operations Command, the Federal Police, and the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Security Directorate. Shortly after arriving at the compound, commanders affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba reportedly ordered their fighters to prevent security personnel from entering. Armed members of the group then surrounded the government force and fired warning shots into the air, forcing the operation to halt.

According to the officials, the PMF leadership subsequently instructed its personnel to withdraw, stating they had not been informed that the target was a facility affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba. Army units involved in the operation later received similar withdrawal orders. No casualties were reported, and neither the government nor the armed group publicly disclosed details of the incident at the time.

The incident comes as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that all weapons in Iraq are brought under state control by September 30, the scheduled end of the U.S.-led coalition’s military mission in the country.

Al-Monitor described the failed operation as the first significant field test of the government’s commitment to enforcing that pledge. While previous administrations also announced plans to limit weapons to state institutions, implementation has remained difficult due to the political and military influence of several armed factions.

Hayder al-Shakeri, a researcher with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, told Al-Monitor that although Baghdad has increasingly relied on restructuring security institutions and applying political and financial pressure on armed groups, the Jurf al-Naddaf operation demonstrated the limits of the state’s authority when confronted directly.

“If the government cannot enforce its decisions against a single armed faction, or fails to follow through with legal and political accountability, it suggests that these groups still retain an effective veto over certain state actions,” Al-Shakeri was quoted as saying.

The report noted that not all Iran-aligned factions share the same position regarding government efforts to centralize weapons under state control.

Some groups, including Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have become increasingly integrated into Iraq’s political and economic systems, potentially reducing their willingness to engage in direct confrontation. Others—including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada—continue to oppose any move that would place their military capabilities under full government authority.

Political analyst Muhannad al-Ghazi told Al-Monitor that these factions view their weapons through an ideological lens, making voluntary disarmament highly unlikely. He argued that targeting isolated weapons caches without addressing broader military infrastructure would have only a limited impact.

The reported confrontation occurred amid heightened regional tensions following Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington, where Iraq and the United States announced a strategic economic partnership.

According to Al-Monitor, several Iran-backed factions criticized the visit, warning against what they described as replacing “military occupation” with “economic occupation” through expanded U.S. investment in Iraq.

The report also linked the incident to broader regional developments, including recent drone attacks and cross-border military operations that have intensified pressure on Baghdad’s efforts to assert control over its territory.

Al-Monitor concluded that the government’s September 30 target for fully disarming armed factions appears increasingly difficult to achieve given current realities.

Instead, analysts cited by the publication believe Baghdad may focus on more gradual measures, including relocating some weapons, closing selected facilities, and increasing political and financial pressure on groups willing to cooperate, while avoiding direct confrontation with the most heavily armed factions.

The report suggested that the ultimate success of Iraq’s disarmament strategy may depend not only on domestic enforcement but also on broader regional dynamics, particularly relations between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Jordan threatens to strike Iranian militias in Iraq if they launched attacks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amman has publicly warned Iraq that it will launch military operations against Iran-backed militias if they attack Jordan.

The warning comes after a rapid increase in regional violence, including recent interceptions of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones over Jordanian airspace, which targeted US installations.

An official Jordanian source told Al-Arabiya News that Jordan provided Iraq with precise intelligence indicating that pro-Iran militants are planning to strike Jordanian territory.

Jordan has publicly said that it expects the Iraqi government to take quick and effective measures to curb these armed groups.

Jordanian sources identify front organizations such as Awliya al-Dam as key players in these border-threatening actions.

The warning represents a strong change in Jordan’s defensive stance in the face of rising tensions between the United States and Iran.

Jordan harbors critical Western military installations, such as the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which have become active targets for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its allies in the region.

Jordan emphasized that, while it aims to avoid regional escalation, it considers national sovereignty and border security to be inviolable priorities.

Following protests by the wrestlers at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in 2023, Delhi Police registered an FIR and later filed a nearly 1,500-page chargesheet against Brij Bhushan, invoking provisions related to sexual harassment, assault or criminal force against a woman, stalking and criminal intimidation under the Indian Penal Code.Tomar was also named as a co-accused.After hearing final arguments from both the prosecution and the defence, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) Ashwani Panwar had reserved the judgment last month. World.title: A race to save 23 sperms, and a teen cancer survivor’s chance at fatherhood
World.content:
For a 19-year-old battling testicular cancer, survival was only one part of the fight. The other was far more personal.

After surgeons removed his only remaining testis, a team of 10 specialists at Mumbaiâs Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital came together on July 25, 2026 with a singular mission â to comb through the nearly dead organ to finding any surviving sperms.

While the surgery to remove the testis was lifesaving, it threatened to end the teenagerâs (his identity has been withheld on familyâs request) chance of becoming a biological father.

The odds that the team of surgeons, urologists, andrologists, fertility specialists and embryologists would find any surviving sperms in the surgically removed testis were daunting. But after hours of meticulous search, there was success â they found 23 viable sperms.

The cells were frozen and preserved for future use. What had begun as an attempt to save a life, ended with the hope of a new one taking birth sometime in the future.

A childhood condition

The teenâs medical journey had begun long before his cancer diagnosis. He was born with cryptorchidism (undescended testes) â a condition in which both testes fail to descend into the scrotum before birth and remain inside the abdomen.

Since the testes require a cooler environment for normal sperm production, the condition can impair fertility and is also associated with an increased risk of testicular cancer.





When he was just a year old, he underwent orchiopexy, a procedure to bring the testes into the scrotum. However, one testis had already sustained irreversible damage and had to be removed. The other was successfully brought down into the scrotum.

Some years later, this surviving testis developed swelling. Investigations revealed a large tumour that had affected nearly 95% of the organ. Removing the cancerous testis became essential to save his life.

But for the teenager, the surgery carried a devastating consequence â it would permanently end his bodyâs ability to produce sperms. âHis case was extremely challenging. We wanted to explore every possible option to preserve his fertility and give him a chance of biological fatherhood,â said Dr Firuza Parikh, director of IVF at Well Women and Menâs Centre, Sir H N Reliance Foundation Hospital.

When every routine option failed

Before the surgery, the patient provided two semen samples.

Both were analysed using an advanced AI-assisted sperm detection system.

âWe have the latest technology to search for sperm in cryptozoospermia â a condition in which sperm are present in extremely low numbers and may not be detected during routine semen analysis, requiring microscopic examination to find them. The technology, the first of its kind in India, was developed in collaboration with the AZ-VUB IVF team in Belgium,â Dr Parikh explained.

Yet, despite the advanced analysis, the results brought heartbreaking news â not a single sperm could be located in the two samples. This medical condition is called azoospermia, meaning a person ejaculates a normal-looking fluid, but the fluid contains zero sperm cells.

âThis was a major setback for us, the family was devastated... now the only option left was to attempt Onco-TESE (oncological testicular sperm extraction) â a specialised fertility preservation technique used in cancer patients,â she said.

The team decided to attempt a rare âex-vivo Onco-TESEâ, a procedure in which sperm retrieval is performed after the cancer-affected testis has been surgically removed. The organ is examined outside the body in a controlled laboratory environment to identify any surviving sperm-producing tissue untouched by the tumour.

A

race

against the clock

On July 25, surgical oncologists Dr Raman Deshpande and Dr Soumil Vyas removed the cancer-affected testis.

Now, the team had just five to six hours to locate and extract the sperms.

A team led by consultant andrologists Dr Rupin Shah and Dr Himanshu Gohil dissected small pieces of tissue surrounding the tumour in search of any surviving tissue. The doctors relied on ultrasound and MRI scans to guide them towards the tiny regions that might still contain viable tissue.

These healthy tissues were then sent to the hospitalâs IVF laboratory.

âHealthy tissue fractions were carefully separated. Once the required tissue fractions were identified, they were placed in a specialised sterile transport medium to maintain tissue viability and preserve any potential viable sperm cells. Prompt processing is critical, as it provides the best chance of preserving any surviving sperm cells.

â

Embryologists led by Dr Varsha Kuril spent five hours going through the tissues for signs of surviving sperms.

When the team identified the first viable sperm cell, they knew they were onto a special moment in medical history. By the time they were done, the team had identified 23 sperms, which were then cryopreserved.

Twenty-three shots at fatherhood

âTwenty-three may sound like a disappointingly small number in the world of sperm counts, where a healthy male can produce millions of sperm cells. But in this case, every single one was a victory â each cell represented a possibility that cancer had nearly taken away,â said Dr Parikh, adding that doctors âwill wait for the time when this young boy gets married and wishes to have children.

Then the sperm will be thawed and used for IVF.

â

According to Dr Tarang Gianchandani, chief executive officer of the hospital, the procedure marked a significant milestone for the institution. âWe have been freezing eggs and ovarian tissue in women with cancer for a long time, but this was the first time that we could get testicular tissue from a testis that was almost entirely destroyed by cancer. And we succeeded only because of our teamâs efforts,â she said.

World.title: 2 strategic satellites sit at spaceport as govt nod eludes Isro
World.content:
GSLV-Mk2

BENGALURU: Two strategically important satellites, NVS-03 and Gisat-1A, have been sitting at Indiaâs spaceport in Sriharikota for weeks, awaiting govt approval for launch. Also waiting is a GSLV-Mk2 rocket, whose propellant filling was halted midway after launch clearance failed to come through, multiple sources told TOI.The delay comes even as the govt is yet to publicly disclose detailed findings into the failures of two PSLV missions â May 18, 2025 and Jan 12, 2026 â that have effectively slowed Indiaâs launch programme across vehicle families.Sources said NVS-03, the next satellite in India's second-generation NavIC navigation constellation, and GISAT-1A or EOS-05, an advanced geo-imaging satellite capable of near real-time observation of the Indian landmass, have both completed most pre-launch preparations and are ready for flight.The GSLV-Mk2 at the spaceport was designated for one of the missions (NVS-03 or Gisat-1A). The pause in launch follows a difficult year for Isro. On Jan 12, PSLV-C62 failed to place its payloads into orbit after a disruption in the third stage (PS3).Eight months before that, PSLV-C61 had also failed because of what Isro has described only as a âpressure drop in PS3â. Apart from these brief descriptions, neither the department of space (DoS) nor the Govt has released detailed failure reports.Union minister Jitendra Singh recently said in Bengaluru that the failure analysis committee investigating the PSLV-C62 mission had identified the cause of the anomaly but that the findings âcould not be disclosed publiclyâ.The apparent caution extending beyond PSLV has befuddled even those within the Department of Space, which is already battling low morale. Officials familiar with the matter said no launches have been cleared while the govt reviews the situation.Pointing out that the issues identified so far relate specifically to the PSLVâs third stage and do not directly involve either the GSLV or the LVM-3, one insider said: âWe donât get the logic. Itâs like telling us not to take our cars out because our bike had an issue in its previous outing.â The person argued that GSLV and LVM rockets donât borrow anything from the PSLV third stage.The delay is particularly significant because both satellites have strategic roles. NVS-03 is expected to be one step in reviving the now-defunct NavIC navigation constellation. Even the govt last week admitted that with just three functional satellites, the NavIC programme has failed to deliver navigation services for lack of satellites.Gisat-1A, meanwhile, revives a mission that has suffered repeated setbacks. The original Gisat-1, Indiaâs first geostationary Earth observation satellite designed to provide frequent imaging of the subcontinent, was first delayed in 2020 before being lost during the GSLV-F10 mission in Aug 2021 after the cryogenic upper stage failed to ignite. The replacement spacecraft is expected to provide near real-time imaging for disaster management, agriculture, forestry, environmental monitoring and national security.The govtâs caution follows another major setback that was investigated in detail. Isro, in Feb this year, released partial findings into the Jan 2025 NVS-02 anomaly, concluding that the spacecraft failed to reach its intended orbit because the drive signal never reached the pyro valve in the oxidiser line during orbit-raising manoeuvres.The agency said corrective measures had since been implemented and successfully validated on the CMS-03 mission launched aboard LVM-3 in Nov 2025. For now, however, even as hardware, satellites and launch vehicles stand ready at the spaceport, Indiaâs next launches remain on hold, with no indication of when the govt will authorise launches to resume.

World.title: MP Pappu Yadav attacked at home during presser
World.content:
NEW DELHI: High drama unfolded at the New Delhi address of Independent MP

Sunday after a man allegedly threw a slipper at him and another allegedly brandished a knife when he was holding a news conference.

The accused, identified by sources as Sumit and Happy Sharma, are from Bulandshahr in UP. Police have detained Sumit (34), and are probing Happyâs role. They are verifying if Happy was the one who threw a slipper at the MP, and if Sumit, who runs a hardware shop, brandished a knife at the event.

The attack is believed to be linked to Yadavâs recent skit outside Parliament over the alleged donation theft at the Ayodhya Ram temple.

On July 31, Opposition MPs staged a skit outside Parliament to protest on the issue, during which Yadav, dressed as a priest, was seen putting donation money in his pocket. MP Bansuri Swaraj complained to police Saturday on the matter.

Sundayâs videos show someone throwing a slipper at Yadav. Moments later, chaos erupts and chairs fly as supporters rush to overpower the men, and police step in. Members of Yadavâs team displayed before reporters the slipper and a knife which, they alleged, were used in the attack.





Yadav alleged that it was a planned attempt on his life. âWhen the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result,â Zaid, MP Yadavâs media convener, claimed.

World.title: Highway deaths dip in India for 1st time since Covid
World.content:
NEW DELHI: For the first time since the Covid pandemic, fatalities on national highways (NHs) declined last year, even as overall road deaths rose in India. Govt data submitted in Lok Sabha last week shows that deaths on NHs, including Centre-run expressways, fell by 4.1% to 62,122 in 2025 from 64,772 in 2024.

Among states and UTs, 20 recorded a decline in fatalities on NHs while 15 reported an increase. Lakshadweep, with no national highways, was the only one to record âzero NH fatalitiesâ since 2022.

Data shows UP registered the steepest decline in NH deaths, with fatalities dropping from 9,560 in 2024 to 7,573 in 2025. Madhya Pradesh also reported a significant reduction, from 4,644 to 3,610, along with Punjab, which logged a sharp fall from 1,562 to 1,022 during the same period.

States that witnessed a rise in NH fatalities include Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Gujarat.

World.title: Youth quitting drugs real warriors: PM on national drive
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Drugs can give a momentary high but family and professional lives will hit a low, PM Modi told youth in a warning against substance abuse on Sunday, and exhorted families not to hide any addiction in the name of social prestige but reach out to experts and cultivate a culture of frank communication with kids.

Launching âNasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyanâ (campaign for drug-free youth for developed India), Modi called for rejecting stigma on the issue. âYouth who come out fighting addiction are not weak; they are real warriors,â he said.

Give drug survivors a second chance, respect them: PM Modi

PM Modi said society should instead respect those who overcome their drug addiction. âThey are real warriors whose incredible courage is their true identity,â he said in a virtual address, with a host of chief ministers, governors, spiritual figures and a large number of youngsters joining the event from across the country.

As the nation has set the goal of âViksit Bharatâ, it is imperative that the countryâs youth remain physically and mentally fit, steering clear of destructive habits like drugs, he said, stressing the importance of support system offered by the society besides the help from yoga and meditation.

He said, âEven if a youth has mistakenly fallen into the trap of addiction, it absolutely does not mean that all doors are closed for them.â





Society should respect them, embrace them and give them a second chance, he said.

Substance abuse has long been a serious concern in parts of the north-east and Punjab, where it has become a major plank for all political parties in the run-up to elections early next year.

Modi noted enemy countries use the supply of drugs as part of their terror plans because they know that youth are the future of country.

The campaign will continue for the next 100 weeks, and every Sunday, activities related to art, culture, sports, meditation, spirituality and services will be organised to take the message of de-addiction to new people.

Family members live with this pain every day, watching their children gradually lose themselves before their eyes, he said. Strict action is being taken against drug traffickers across the country. The arrests have gone up several times, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized, the PM said.

World.title: NTA floats tender to secure offices, exam material 24x7
World.content:
NEW DELHI: After a paper leak exposed weak links in Indiaâs biggest entrance examination,

(

) is moving to put its premises, confidential records and examination material under round-the-clock watch.

The agency has floated a tender estimated at Rs 7.5 crore to hire a security firm for its headquarters at Minto Road, regional office in Okhla and other notified locations.

Issued on July 25, the tender is part of a procurement exercise covering security, housekeeping and examination-grade printing. Together, the bids signal an attempt to tighten controls across the examination chain â from printing and storage to access control and protection of digital infrastructure.

The security contract will initially run for two years and may be extended twice by a year each. Bids can be submitted until 3 pm on Aug 17.

The printing-services tender closes on Aug 20.

The selected agency will watch over NTA employees, visitors, premises, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms, warehouses, record rooms and other sensitive facilities. It will regulate entry and exit, verify staff and visitors, maintain logs and ensure that âonly authorised persons enter restricted areasâ.





The security apparatus will include door-frame and hand-held metal detectors, GPS-enabled guard patrol tracking, biometric attendance and digital incident-reporting systems.

NTA has moved away from choosing a bidder mainly on cost basis. Citing the âsensitive nature of NTAâs examination ecosystem and confidentiality requirementsâ, it has adopted the quality-and-cost based selection model. Technical capability will carry 70% weightage and the financial bid 30%.

Only agencies securing at least 70 marks in the technical assessment will reach the financial round.

Bidders must have at least five yearsâ experience in professional security, an average annual turnover of Rs 10 crore in past three financial years and must have done prior work at high-security establishments such as central govt institutions, examination agencies, universities, airports, hospitals or metro systems.

Bidders for NTA tender will have to deposit 15 lakh as earnest money

The contract value excludes GST. Bidders must deposit Rs 15 lakh as earnest money, while the successful agency will furnish performance security equal to 5% of the contract value.

Confidentiality is mandatory. The service provider and its personnel must protect information relating to examination material, security arrangements and IT systems even after the contract ends.

The tender has been floated amid efforts to rebuild public confidence after the NEET controversy and have a foolproof system in place against paper leaks. The exercise suggests that NTA is treating security as a process in which every access point can become a vulnerability.

World.title: 10,000 cases pending in SC for 10 yrs, 80,000 in HCs for 30 yrs
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Improving court infrastructure and integration of technology in the justice delivery system with an outlay of more than Rs 9,800 crore since 2011 have had little impact on disposal of cases pending for several decades. More than 10,000 cases are pending in the Supreme Court for over 10 years â including 558 pending for over 20 years, and 26 cases for 30 years. In the 25 high courts across the country, over 80,000 cases are pending for over three decades.In a written response to a question in Parliament last week, law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal put the onus of disposal of cases on the judiciary, which has not fixed a time frame for their disposal.He further said: âTimely disposal of cases in courts depends on several factors which, inter-alia, include availability of adequate number of judges and judicial officers, supporting court staff and physical infrastructure, complexity of facts involved, nature of evidence, cooperation of stakeholders viz bar, investigation agencies, witnesses, litigants and proper application of rules and procedures.âWhile the apex court has been prompt in appointing judges against vacancies, the situation in 25 high courts and subordinate courts is not the same.The HCs currently have 341 vacancies of judges against a sanctioned strength of 1,122. The subordinate courts have 7,311 vacancies against an approved strength of 30,868 judges.The law minister blamed the respective HC collegiums for not following the timeline prescribed for initiating recommendation for appointments of judges for the HCs, the primary reason behind large vacancies. The HC collegium comprises the chief justice and two senior-most judges of the high court. For the SC, the recommendation for the appointment of judges is initiated by the Chief Justice of India.âArrears Committees have been set up in all 25 high courts and the district courts to clear cases pending for more than five years. The govt has also enacted the New Criminal Laws 2023, Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018, Commercial Courts (Amendment) Act, 2018, Specific Relief (Amendment) Act, 2018 with a view to reduce pendency,â Meghwal said.

World.title: Ujjaini Mahankali Rangam 2026: Oracle predicts heavy rains in Telangana, warns of fires, accidents and loss of lives
World.content:
The annual Rangam (soothsayer ritual) at the Sri Ujjaini Mahankali Temple in Secunderabad on Monday (August 3, 2026), saw the oracle forecast heavy rainfall across Telangana during the year, while warning of fire incidents, accidents and possible loss of lives. The oracle also expressed displeasure over an unfulfilled promise concerning the Goddess’ idol.

What is Rangam?

Rangam, one of the key rituals associated with the Ujjaini Mahankali Bonalu celebrations, is traditionally held on the Monday following the main festivities. During the ritual, the oracle stands atop an earthen pot and delivers the Bhavishyavani (prophecy), which traditionally touches upon rainfall, agriculture, public welfare and developments expected during the year.

Heavy rains forecast

A significant part of the prophecy centred on the weather, with the oracle forecasting heavy rains and urging people to exercise caution. She indicated that some spells of rainfall could be particularly intense and also referred to the possibility of uneven distribution, with some places receiving inadequate rain even as others witness heavy downpours.

The oracle also warned of fire-related incidents and accidents and cautioned that some incidents could result in loss of lives. Referring to growing conflicts among people, she said people were increasingly fighting among themselves and warned that such confrontations could have serious consequences.

Be responsible towards parents

The prophecy also touched upon social issues, particularly the conduct of young people and their relationship with their parents. The oracle called for the youth to be guided on the right path and encouraged to live in harmony with one another. She also criticised those who, after becoming successful, leave their parents behind in their native villages and become arrogant, urging them to shed their pride and remain mindful of their responsibilities towards their parents.

Unfulfilled promise

The oracle also expressed dissatisfaction over the manner in which certain rituals and offerings were being performed. While saying that she continued to provide advice, solutions and blessings to devotees, she indicated that some obligations towards the Goddess were not being fulfilled to her satisfaction. Reiterating her displeasure over an unfulfilled promise concerning the Goddess’ idol, the oracle warned temple representatives against delaying the matter further and sought its fulfilment within 3 to 6 months.

World.title: What’s at stake in the latest U.S.-Iran talks?
World.content:
After 156 days of war and one Memorandum of Understanding between Iran and U.S., President Donald Trump on Sunday (August 2, 2026) said the American forces have called off military strikes against Iran on the request of Gulf allies. Mr. Trump announced the development, referring to his allies Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.

Mr. Trump told the U.S. forces had plans in place to carry out the “biggest attack since World War II”. However, he has set the plan aside and give diplomacy a fair chance on the request of key Gulf leaders, including Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and other Iranian officials. “I said to the Crown Prince, ‘What would you rather do? Would you rather us do this or not?’ Mr. Trump told reporters on Air Force One as he flew back to Washington after spending the weekend at his golf club in Bedminster, New Jersey. “They said we would much prefer a deal as opposed to an attack, because you don’t know where these attacks lead.”

In a sharp rebuttal, the Iranian news agency Mehr, citing Iranian military officials, said the allegation “was nothing but a new lie”.

The announcement of a fresh round of talks between U.S. and Iran has leased a fresh hope in the global order, with expectation for an immediate ceasefire soon. The agreement arrives a little more than a month after Iran and U.S. signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to end the war.

Here are the key developments essential to understanding why the upcoming round of talks between Iran and U.S. officials is important.

The Lebanon issue

The military hostility in Lebanon, especially southern Lebanon, did not see any restraint owing to the nature of June 15 agreement between U.S. and Iran. Typically a Hezbollah stronghold, Israel captures parts of Southern Lebanon, triggering regular instances of military strike in the area. The equation is complex since Iran maintains a close relationship with Hezbollah, a Lebanese Shia militia-cum-political party.

In the past, Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz have said Israel will not retreat its forces from the region. Significantly, the ceasefire talks between Iran and Israel have been called off on multiple instances owing to Israel’s military aggression.

Strait of Hormuz factor

The biggest immediate stake is the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil trade normally passes. Disruptions in the waterway have rattled global energy markets, pushed up freight costs and fuelled inflation fears. Any agreement that restores normal shipping could ease pressure on oil prices and improve global economic confidence. Even though, Iran has claimed the waterway if off-limits due to ongoing military tension. However, the U.S. has claimed the closure claims to be false. The flashpoint has triggered a disruption in global supply of essential goods and increasing prices on it.

Rising crude oil price

The continue rise in oil prices had disrupted the economy of major nations. Higher crude costs increase the price of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel, raise transportation and manufacturing expenses, and feed into inflation across economies. For oil-importing countries such as India, which meets more than 85% of its crude oil requirement through imports, expensive oil widens the import bill, puts pressure on the rupee, increases the current account deficit and complicates fiscal management. Central banks may also find it harder to contain inflation, potentially delaying interest-rate cuts and slowing economic growth.

World.title: SP legislators protest in Uttar Pradesh Assembly premises over Ram temple donation issue
World.content:
SP legislators on Monday (August 3, 2026) staged a protest in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly premises, accusing the BJP government of failing to act on the Ram temple donation theft issue and demanding action over paper leaks.

Holding placards that read "NEET hai ya cheat hai" (Is it NEET or cheat), "Daan ka paisa kahan milega, BJP ke khate me" (Donation money will be found in BJP's account)", the Samajwadi Party (SP) MLAs and MLCs alleged that the government was attempting to suppress the truth in the Ram temple donation matter and sought a fair probe.

Holding a donation box in their hand, SP MLAs alleged that the BJP had "betrayed the faith of devotees" and demanded accountability over donations made for the temple. They also claimed devotees were losing confidence and sought a transparent investigation.

Issues such as paper leaks, unemployment, inflation, fertiliser shortage, floods and alleged irregularities in reservation should be discussed in the House, they said.

They also accused the government of curtailing the duration of the Monsoon session to avoid debate on public issues.

The protesting legislators said incidents of examination paper leaks had adversely affected students and demanded strict action against those responsible.

The four-day Monsoon Session of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly begins on Monday (August 3, 2026).

World.title: CWG 2026 India’s final medal tally: List of winners and overall table
World.content:
India concluded its campaign at the 23rd Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games in fourth place after securing a total of 39 medals: 13 gold, 17 silver, and nine bronze.

Leading a 122-member contingent across eight able-bodied (athletics, artistic gymnastics, bowls, boxing, judo, swimming, track cycling, weightlifting) and five integrated para-sports categories (para athletics, para powerlifting, para swimming, para track cycling and 3x3 wheelchair basketball), Indian athletes have left their indelible mark in Scotland.

India secured a fourth-place finish at the Commonwealth Games for the second consecutive time, trailing behind Canada.

Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu secured India’s first gold medal in Glasgow by winning the 48 kg event. Meanwhile, Rishikanta Singh won India’s first able-bodied medal with a silver in the Men’s 60 kg weightlifting category, and Raja Muthupandi followed up with a second silver in the Men’s 65 kg weightlifting event.

Para-powerlifter Jhandu Kumar officially opened India’s medal account on Friday (July 24) by capturing a bronze medal in the Men’s para-powerlifting division. India won its second bronze when Bindyarani Devi finished third in the final of the women’s 58 kg weightlifting event.

Asmita Dey made history by winning India's first-ever gold medal in judo at the Commonwealth Games. Shortly after, Harsh Singh also joined the ranks.

Indian boxers delivered strong performances at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, securing 10 medals: 7 gold and 3 silver. This impressive haul of seven gold medals is the most ever won by any nation in boxing at a single edition of the Commonwealth Games, a record that had remained unbeaten for nearly a century.

World.title: Counting underway for Datia Assembly bypoll in Madhya Pradesh; tight security in place
World.content:
Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh was leading by 33 votes, over BJP candidate Ashutosh Tiwari after the third round of counting on Monday (August 3, 2026) for the Datia Assembly bypoll in Madhya Pradesh.

Mr. Singh secured 12,432 votes, while Mr. Tiwari bagged 12,399 votes after the completion of third of 15 rounds of counting, according to ECI website. Aazad Samaj Party’s Damodar Yadav is on the third position with 4,874 votes.

Counting of votes for the bypoll to the Datia Assembly constituency in Madhya Pradesh commenced on Monday (August 3, 2026), officials said.

The counting process began at 8 a.m. at the Polytechnic College under tight security, starting with postal ballots before moving on to Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).

A day before the result of Datia Assembly seat, the Congress suspended former MLA Rajendra Bharti — whose disqualification due to his conviction in a bank fraud case necessitated the bypoll — from the party’s primary membership.

The suspension comes days after the Congress candidate for the bypoll, Mr. Singh, accused Mr. Bharti of trying to sabotage his campaign and colluding with the Bharatiya Janata Party.

The BJP fielded debutant Mr. Tiwari, after snubbing former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra who represented the seat for three consecutive terms until his defeat to Mr. Bharti in the 2023 Assembly polls

Bypoll to the Datia Assembly seat was held on July 30 and recorded a voting turnout of 71.44%, as per the Election Commission.

A total of 21 tables, including 20 for counting of EVMs, were set up at the facility, an official said.

In the 230-member Madhya Pradesh assembly, the BJP has 164 MLAs, the Congress 64 and the Bharat Adivasi Party one legislator.

The Datia bypoll is also the first electoral test for newly appointed BJP state president Hemant Khandelwal.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: West Asia LIVE: Trump says Iran talks to take place today, sets no deadline for deal
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said talks with ‌Iran will happen on Monday (August 3, 2026) but declined to set a deadline for an agreement after earlier saying he had called off an imminent attack in hopes of quickly reaching a deal ⁠to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resolve the impasse over Tehran’s nuclear capabilities.

Mr. Trump had said late on Saturday (August 1, 2026) on his Truth Social platform that Iran and other West Asian countries had asked for time to complete a deal that would lead to “the ‌Immediate, Complete and Total” reopening of the strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat” but that Tehran must “rapidly make a DEAL.”

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held phone calls with his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan and Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir to discuss diplomatic efforts, Iran’s state media reported on Sunday (August 2, 2026). World.title: Prosthetic hand camps to be held in all Andhra Pradesh districts by year-end
World.content:
In a significant step towards empowering persons with disabilities, the AP Red Cross Society, in collaboration with Rotary International and supported by the Tangience Foundation, USA, organised a special prosthetic hand-fitting camp in Guntur on Sunday (August 2, 2026). The camp provided advanced imported LN4 prosthetic hands to around 200 beneficiaries, helping them regain independence and improve their quality of life.

The beneficiaries were identified after extensive outreach by Red Cross teams across Guntur, Krishna, Prakasam and West Godavari districts. Of the applicants screened, 255 persons who had lost their hands or forearms in accidents or because of congenital conditions were found eligible for prosthetic hand fitting.

Organisers said the LN4 prosthetic hands would enable users to perform routine tasks independently, boosting their confidence and opening opportunities for education, employment and sustainable livelihoods. Beneficiaries are also receiving practical training on the proper use and maintenance of the devices to ensure effective adaptation.

Expressing gratitude, beneficiaries said the prosthetic hands would help them overcome physical limitations and lead more self-reliant and productive lives.

The programme was attended by Rotary District 3150 Governor Rtn. Uday Sudhir Pilani, AP Red Cross Chairman Y.D. Rama Rao, General Secretary A.K. Parida, Guntur Red Cross Chairman Rtn. Vadlamani Ravi, AP Red Cross Vice Chairman Rtn. P. Ramachandra Raju and other dignitaries.

The organisers described the camp as the first of its kind this year and announced plans to conduct similar camps across all districts in Andhra Pradesh by year-end to provide prosthetic hands to every eligible beneficiary on a saturation basis.

World.title: PML-N bags 14 seats in 2nd phase of AJK polls amid allegations of rigging
World.content:
The PML-N has bagged 14 seats while the PPP has managed to secure just four of the total 18 seats that were up for grabs in the second phase of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) election on Sunday, according to unofficial results released by the Election Commission.

Polling was postponed until Tuesday in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) as polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads.

State broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported the unofficial results of 18 seats, citing Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal’s press talk in Muzaffarabad.

During the press talk, he announced that the PML-N had won 14 seats and the PPP four.

Unofficial results

LA-34 bagged by PML-N’s Nasir Dar

LA-35 bagged by PML-N’s Chaudhry Muhammad Ismail

LA-36 bagged by PML-N’s Muhammad Ahsan Raza

LA-37 bagged by PNL-N’s Maryam Javed

LA-38 bagged by PML-N’s Zeeshah Ali

LA-39 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Muhammad Siddique Khan

LA-41 bagged by PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah

LA-30 bagged by PML-N’s Mustafa Bashir Abbasi

LA-31 bagged by PML-N’s Saqib Majeed Khan

LA-32 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Farooq Haider Khan
